prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline. Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Business Rules Registry governs fairness/carriers/spacing/subscriptions/runway-configuration-specific maximum-queue/warning/intervention-thresholds. Cedarbell normalizes against Airport Capacity Plan;Marlinstone predicts stand/apron/runway/departure-fix demand;Capacity Assessment Module compares Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector limits. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;runway/fix/Ground Delay Program constraints;capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Copperfin authorizes Capacity Reduction State exceptions/recovery/divergence;receives rate-erosion notifications;selects metering/delay/rerouting/regulation. Halcyon confirms publication,requests delay/fairness adjustments,checks resequencing/Slot Compliance State. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:advisory movements/timestamped milestones. Quartzline reconciles constraints,sends Stand Tow Request Form;Blueharbor recalculates. Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes capacity endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Lantern distributes approvals. Saffron shall confirm revisions before freeze-horizon;justified connection/crew/rotation reviews

New part:
S378: Ramp Control Lead uses the queue card to verify pad entry order before authorizing a movement from the staging area.
S379: When demand exceeds the safe holding capacity near the pad, the Departure Metering Service withholds further push clearances until the pad queue falls below the configured threshold.
S380: The Tower Sequence Manager reserves departure sequence positions only for aircraft with an achievable pad release time and a valid runway taxi path.
S381: The Airport CDM Portal records the selected fluid type, mixture ratio, treatment start time, treatment completion time, and expected holdover reference for each treated aircraft.
S382: Fluid status updates are timestamped through the Time Synchronization Service so that ramp, tower, and airline users interpret treatment age consistently.
S383: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates remaining fluid inventory and truck serviceability when replenishment, contamination, or equipment faults affect the planned treatment rate.
S384: The Handling Resource Planner compares fluid inventory with scheduled deicing demand and warns when a planned bank cannot be supported without resequencing.
S385: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews aircraft readiness and may request a later pad entry when crew, catering, or passenger status would cause holdover time to be wasted.
S386: Gate Conflict Detector produces the Gate Reopening Memo when a stand becomes usable after snow clearance and the gate occupancy constraint has been removed.
S387: Quartzline must coordinate every pad release with the Tower Supervisor before the aircraft leaves the treated area.
S388: Under freezing conditions, the Tower Supervisor protects runway departure spacing by accounting for reduced braking action, slower lineup, and possible repeat treatment requests.
S389: The Surface Surveillance Adapter confirms that aircraft leaving the pad follow the assigned route and do not block inbound traffic to the same treatment complex.
S390: If a treated aircraft cannot depart within its applicable holdover reference, the Deicing Coordinator marks the treatment as expired and returns the aircraft to the appropriate queue state.
S391: The Common Situation Display highlights expired treatments, pad closures, fluid shortages, and ramp blockages so that participants can resolve conflicts without separate status calls.
S392: The Collaborative Decision Log captures winter-mode decisions, including capacity changes, pad flow restrictions, and agreed deviations from the normal departure order.
S393: When conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager authorizes a controlled transition from Capacity Reduction State toward Recovery Phase after pad backlog, runway condition, and surface flow indicators are stable.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
